item.title: Develop, Deploy, Support and Maintain Existing and Future Citywide Transit Signal Priority (TSP)
item.description:
Transportation | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-10-19

The New York City Department of Transportation (the Agency) seeks a qualified vendor to develop, deploy, support, and maintain existing and future Transit Signal Priority (TSP) corridors. The Agency has successfully deployed a centralized Transit Signal Priority (TSP) System within the Citys five boroughs. Central TSP leverages the existing ITS infrastructure, including a new Traffic Safety Network (TSN), centralized Traffic Control Systems, and on-board bus equipment to lower costs and to facilitate rapid implementation. This minimized the hardware and software required to make the TSP System operational. Existing and future bus corridors on the TSP System span approximately 200 miles and include about 3,500 signalized traffic intersections. Additionally, more corridors are planned/deployed over the next few years. This Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx is released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal. Responses to this RFP/RFx must be submitted via PASSPort. To access the RFP/RFx, vendors should visit the PASSPort Public Portal. item.title: 6 Month NAE with Safe Horizon Inc. for CVAP
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-09-21

On behalf of the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV), the Department Social Services (DSS) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) contract with Safe Horizon, Inc. to extend the contract for the Crime Victims Advocate Program (CVAP) by 6 months. CVAP places victim advocates for survivors of domestic violence and additional advocates for victims of every other category of crime in precincts and Housing Police Service Areas citywide. Advocates provide supportive counseling, connections to individual or group therapy, and help navigating the legal and financial challenges that can emerge after a crime has occurred. CVAP represents the Citys largest single investment in supportive services for victims of crime and regularly reaches more than 40,000 crime victims annually.

The proposed NAE term will be from 1/1/2027 through 6/30/2027 with a contract amount of $9,527,801.88.

Procurement and award are in accordance with PPB Rule Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) for the reasons set forth herein.
